_minClaudeVersionNote: Floor = the lowest claude version measured on a fleet host in XACA-1599-001 (2.1.267, the oldest host at that time). `kb-sync-plugins check --host --probe` is the per-host behavioural probe: it asks a `claude -p` session for the L1 marker and exits 3 when it cannot verify. Record each host's probe result (host, claude version, date, verdict) in kanban/plans/XACA-1599/XACA-1599_006_probe_results.md at rollout. Raise the floor only if a host at the floor fails the probe.
_schemaNote: Schema 2 (XACA-1643): ONE fleet plugin list (`fleet.plugins`) rendered into every team in `teamTargets` by kb-sync-plugins `effective_team_cfg()`. A team block never carries `enabledPlugins` (validation rejects it). A team leaves the fleet list only through an entry in `exceptions`, which must carry a reason. `teams` was renamed `teamTargets` on purpose: a schema-1 script that meets this file fails closed (KeyError, exit 70, nothing written) instead of stripping every owned plugin. Design record: kanban/plans/XACA-1643/XACA-1643_one_fleet_toolset.md.

baseline._note: L1 managed policy, rendered by `kb-sync-plugins managed-policy --print` into managed-settings.d/50-aiteamforge.json. Bump `revision` with every change: it is the AITEAMFORGE_MANAGED_POLICY marker the probe looks for. L1 only blocks (false); it never force-enables a plugin.

swift-lsp@claude-plugins-official.install: Xcode or Command Line Tools (manual): xcode-select --install

pluginClasses.connector: Reaches an external service with the user's account or data, whatever the transport (http MCP, stdio CLI, ...)
pluginClasses.local: Everything else: LSPs, prompt-only plugins, local tools, built-ins

fleet._note: The one fleet plugin list. Every entry MUST carry a `class` (an unclassified entry is a validation error, so a new SaaS plugin cannot reach a personal-data team by being forgotten). A `connector` entry MUST name its `service`. Classification is a recorded human decision: no heuristic can tell firebase (connector) from playwright (local), both are stdio npx MCPs.

freelance.reason: Freelance client work: every registry team matched by the freelance-* pattern in teamTargetPatterns, filled in at load time (user decision 2026-10-28)

platform.reason: Platform/infra teams, and richmond (XACA-1676: fleet-standard set, connectors included): full fleet list incl. connectors (user decision 2026-10-25). Every team target must sit in a group, so a new team forces an explicit connector decision; the other code teams are in the mainevent group below.

mainevent.reason: The mainevent code teams (user decision 2026-10-28). The `mainevent` coordination team has its own teamTargets entry and is deliberately not a member of this PLUGIN group; it does receive the mainevent skills (skills.groups.mainevent, XACA-1643-006).

exceptions.reason: External-service connectors stay off for personal-data teams (finance, legal, medical)
Client data: external-service connectors stay off for freelance teams, the same rule as the personal teams

liveOutOfScope.reason: Mods layer (CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS today, a user-scope marketplace later under XACA-1605): not the team toolset

skills._note: Skill classes (XACA-1643-006, design record D6). `shared` skills are machine-wide on every host and are exactly the sync-tap.sh mirrored list (tests/test-xaca-1643-skills.sh enforces it both ways). `devHost` skills are machine-wide only on hosts with a dev-team clone and stay NOT-MIRRORED, each with its reason. A `groups.<g>` skill is NOT machine-wide: kb-sync-plugins writes project-scope symlinks <session dir>/.claude/skills/<name> -> <owner source root>/<name> into the group's teams' session dirs and linked worktrees (untracked; it never writes inside the owning repo, and removes only symlinks it recorded). `owner` picks the source root from `sourceRoots`; a root is a literal path, `${dev_team}/...`, or `${working_dir:<registry key>}/...` (the registry key's working_dir on this host); skills owned outside this repo are distribution only. deploy-to-production.sh skips every group skill (it reads skills.groups itself; `kb-sync-plugins skills group-names` prints the same list and a test pins that), so a group skill never lands in the machine-wide user skills dir.

Release Manager.reason: Hard-codes a personal absolute path to a dev-host config file (SKILL.md ~L435): that must not ship. Mirror it after the path is removed (spin-out candidate).

LCARS Styling.reason: Guides edits to canonical fleet-monitor CSS, which the tap publisher overwrites, and carries organisation-specific panel examples (SKILL.md 580-639).

Initialize Team.reason: Provisions canonical dev-team infra files through kb-init-team (14 sites; aiteamforge_paths.py is a mirrored canonical file), so it only means something against a dev-team clone.

mainevent.reason: These skills reach only the mainevent teams (user decisions 2026-10-25 and 2026-10-28): a machine-wide copy would hand them to academy, dns and the personal teams.

cab-workflow-audit.reason: Publishes to a customer-specific Confluence space (SKILL.md ~L156): that change-control process belongs to the mainevent teams. Academy-owned, so it stays NOT-MIRRORED and is delivered to the group only.

unmanagedTeams._note: Registry teams deliberately outside the toolset, as {<registry key>: <reason>}. None today: the freelance teams and the second ios repo are managed targets (user decision 2026-10-28).

teamTargetPatterns._note: One pattern stands for every registry team whose key starts with the prefix, expanded at load time by kb-sync-plugins expand_patterns() into ordinary teamTargets entries (and into the `teams` of the group named here), so this file names no client or project team. A pattern's dirs must all be `${working_dir}` (each expanded team's own registry dir). A pattern that can match a personal or client-data team must route to a noConnectors group (validation enforces it, and the same hard floor applies to every expanded name).
